scope: SCOPED: atomic IPv4 datagram definition, arbitrary sender Identification and receiver ignoring Identification in the unfragmented IPv4 codec/quoted-header decoder. Updates RFC791 and RFC1122 Identification semantics. No full-document or full IPv4 host conformance: non-atomic datagrams, fragmentation/reassembly, non-atomic ID allocation/rate limits, forwarding, NAT and tunnel behavior are outside this inventory.

paragraphs.reason: Encoder emits exactly DF=1, MF=0 and zero fragment offset. Assertions inspect all 16 flag/offset bits, not just DF.

paragraphs.quote: The IPv4 ID field MUST NOT be used for purposes other than fragmentation and reassembly.
paragraphs.reason: In the selected unfragmented codec, no packet metadata, option handling or payload result depends on ID. Checksum-correct distinct-ID packets have equal parse and quote results; non-atomic reassembly is unsupported.

paragraphs.quote: Originating sources MAY set the IPv4 ID field of atomic datagrams to any value.
paragraphs.reason: The selected sender chooses zero for every atomic datagram, including different payloads; no per-flow ID uniqueness mechanism is needed or claimed.

paragraphs.quote: All devices that examine IPv4 headers MUST ignore the IPv4 ID field of atomic datagrams.
paragraphs.reason: Both live and quoted-header decoders ignore ID semantically while still verifying the header checksum. The test reseals the checksum for multiple ID values and compares every exposed field, options and payload.

paragraphs.quote: Sources emitting non-atomic datagrams MUST NOT repeat IPv4 ID values within one MDL for a given source address/destination address/protocol tuple.
paragraphs.reason: This remaining uniqueness rule is retained as an explicit unsupported capability boundary. The encoder only emits atomic datagrams; no non-atomic ID allocator or reassembly support is claimed.
